title: Post-incident follow-up: damp GPU pool 'resonant' queue growth, calibrate soft-throttle & circuit-breaker margins
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-03-07 hosted API capacity event we observed repeated fast-growing request queues on several GPU pools which then triggered aggressive pool-wide throttling. The primary failure mode is an interaction between our recent prewarm/hysteresis changes and tenant admission scoring that produced a positive feedback loop: latency spikes increased admission backlog, backlog increased prewarm pressure, prewarm churn consumed spare capacity, and autoscaler reacted too slowly leading to sustained saturation.

This ticket captures follow-ups and implements non-invasive mitigations to prevent recurrence while we iterate on longer-term fixes (smarter autoscaler, KV cache prioritization, and tenant fairness). The goal is to remove the resonant amplification and ensure graceful degradation for high-traffic tenants.

Root cause (concise):
- A hysteresis parameter change reduced the cooldown window on idle gpus, increasing prewarm activity at the start of bursts.
- Admission scoring favored throughput for some tenants and allowed bursts to monopolize queue slots during priming.
- Autoscaler decision latency (30–90s) was insufficient for short, high-intensity bursts; we observed cumulative latency > 200s before new capacity was ready.
- Observability gaps: per-tenant queue depth was not visible in the primary SLO dashboard, delaying detection.

Impact observed:
- 14% of requests during the window hit soft-throttle policy (synthetic 429-equivalent), with higher tail latency for affected tenants.
- Two enterprise customers experienced degraded response times for 11 minutes with customer-facing errors for 2 of them (escalated to SRE).

Decision summary / tradeoffs: 
- Short-term mitigations must be low-risk to shipping runtime and not require model re-quantization or heavy kernel changes.
- We prefer admission-side controls and prewarm smoothing rather than drastic autoscaler configuration changes that could increase cost.
- Longer-term work (autoscaler redesign and KV cache priority lanes) will be tracked separately; this ticket implements medium-term operational controls and observability fixes.

Acceptance criteria:
- New soft-throttle margin introduced and validated in canary pools reduces queue amplification factor by >= 4x for synthetic burst tests (see dashboard links).
- A fast admission-circuit breaker that drops >95% of new burst-originated admission at 90th percentile when pool saturation is detected (configurable per pool) deployed to 2 canary pools and validated for 48 hours.
- Per-tenant queue depth surface added to the SLO dashboard and an alert when any tenant's queue depth exceeds 75% of pool fair-share for >30s.
- Runbook updated with clear rollback steps and a pre-approval matrix for emergency parameter changes.
action_items: A1: Implement soft-throttle damping coefficient and expose as pool-level knob (owner: Priya Nair) - due 2026-03-17
A2: Build admission circuit-breaker that measures incoming burst slope and trips before prewarm begins (owner: Michael Ortega) - due 2026-03-18
A3: Add per-tenant queue-depth metric to hosted-api SLO dashboard and create PagerDuty alert (owner: SRE team, contact: Jenna Liu) - due 2026-03-15
A4: Create canary plan and run synthetic replay tests against canary pools with traffic shapes from the incident (owner: Performance team) - due 2026-03-16
A5: Short-run autoscaler tuning: reduce decision window for canary pools to 15s and enable opportunistic prewarm holdback (owner: Autoscale team) - due 2026-03-19
A6: Post-deploy retrospective with metrics and annotated trace of the next 3 incidents (owner: Alex Kim) - due 2026-03-26
comments: 2026-03-10 Alex Kim: Created ticket after cross-team postmortem. Initial plan favors admission-side damping and observability fixes. Assigned to Priya to implement soft-throttle knob.

2026-03-11 Priya Nair: Implemented soft-throttle coefficient and added feature flag. Deployed to test cluster; initial synthetic replay shows queue slope reduced by ~3.2x. Need to tune per-pool defaults.

2026-03-12 Michael Ortega: Prototype of admission circuit-breaker landed in branch and running against canary, see PR. Early trials show trips occurring earlier than desired for multi-tenant bursts; adjusting detection window.
2026-03-12 Jenna Liu (SRE): Per-tenant queue metric added to telemetry pipeline and visible on internal dashboard. PagerDuty rule created for sustained per-tenant queue > 75% of fair-share.
2026-03-13 Alex Kim: Decision to prioritize canary rollouts with reduced autoscaler decision window for 2 pools. Monitoring window extended to 72 hours for canaries before wider rollout.

2026-03-13 Operations note: Emergency rollback path documented: disable soft-throttle flag and revert autoscaler window via infra-ops orchestration script. Contact SRE oncall if any major regressions observed.
